result.title: UMM-JEPA: Generative Pretraining via Masked Next-Scale Representation Prediction for Unified Multimodal Models
result.summary: Unified multimodal models can support both visual understanding and generation, yet generative training does not necessarily improve understanding. We argue that this limitation may arise from a mismatch between the representation targeted by generation and the perceptual representation used for understanding. Conventional generation objectives primarily optimize synthesis-oriented spaces such as discrete visual codes or generative latents. We therefore introduce UMM-JEPA, which reformulates generation as progressive prediction of continuous visual-understanding representations. The model constructs a multi-scale representation hierarchy from coarse to fine, while pixel rendering is decoupled from representation pretraining and attached only afterward. Controlled comparisons show that the representation-prediction objective accounts for most of the understanding improvement, while a data-matched control leaves the group means nearly unchanged. UMM-JEPA reaches a 16-benchmark visual mean of 51.71, against 46.36 for the understanding-only Qwen-VL baseline, and the text mean also rises. Compared with discrete-code and latent-flow generation objectives, perceptual representation prediction yields stronger and more consistent transfer to understanding. Linear probes and visual-evidence interventions further reveal richer object and spatial structure and stronger use of image-specific information. These results suggest that generation can benefit understanding when it directly supervises the perceptual representations that understanding consumes.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 UMM-JEPA，把统一多模态模型的生成训练改为对连续视觉理解表征做由粗到细的多尺度渐进预测，并将像素渲染解耦后置，再以控制实验、线性探针和视觉证据干预比较其与离散 code、latent flow 目标的迁移差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 它直指「生成所监督的表征与理解所消费的视觉表征不匹配」这一 LVR 核心问题，其多尺度表征预测目标与图像特定信息使用分析可供核查生成 latent 是否保留并用于任务必要的视觉细节；但研究的是训练目标而非推理期 latent 状态生成。
